code_base: daily-scale 13320c6 + karst/daily_bench.py (daily path unchanged; phases measured by wrapping existing functions, exclusive time)
command: python -m karst.daily_bench --members 10 --members 50 --members 200 [--price-delay S] [--news-delay S] [--failure-rate P] [--no-news] [--news-items K] [--prior-news K] [--history-bars B]

local_benchmark.environment: Windows 11, Python 3.12.10, local SSD; fake Longbridge (4 calls/member, 1000 bars at registration, only bars since the window on the daily run) and fake RSS (2 feeds/member, 5 new articles/feed + 1 shared market article, 20 prior articles/feed registered first). No network.
local_benchmark.note: N=10/50 from a clean rerun; N=200 from a run that did not overlap the test suite. Seconds are totals over the run; 'other' = wall minus measured phases (registry lock, record_refresh, JSON of results, loop).

runs.delays: price 0.25 s/call (x4), news 0.8 s/feed (2 feeds in parallel), failure rate 0.02, seed 7
runs.reading: Injected waits add one-for-one to wall time (50 x (1.0 + 0.8) s = 90 s of 99 s fetch): members are strictly sequential.

quadratic_total (per-member cost grows w.index_store: 31 -> 74 -> 236 ms/member. store.index_text checks 'SELECT 1 FROM evidence_text WHERE evidence_id=?' on the FTS5 virtual table; that column is not indexed, so every new record scans all indexed text rows of every company. It also grows day by day as evidence accumulates, not only with N.
quadratic_total (per-member cost grows w.checkpoint: 3 -> 9 -> 32 ms/member. daily._save_run rewrites the whole receipt (all results so far) after every member: 156 MB serialized for N=200. The same full receipt is returned by the MCP call.

growth_with_members.per_company_history (grows with days kep: register_evidence / read_registry: every register re-reads and schema-validates the company's whole manifest, rewrites it with fsync and rewrites observations.jsonl. Cost per article rises with each company's accumulated evidence.

local_benchmark.peak_memory: Peak RSS 81-86 MB for N=10..200; the refresh adds < 3 MB. Memory is not a constraint.

cloud_measurement.tool: mcp__karst__refresh_daily_scope(universe_id='daily-monitoring'), no since; no record_update_check / save / publish called
cloud_measurement.intake_status: ready_for_review (10/10, no failure, no history recovery)
cloud_measurement.mcp_response_note: The call returned but its 246 KB result exceeded the Claude Code tool-result limit and was spilled to a file; the full receipt is returned inline.
cloud_measurement.per_member_method: Difference between consecutive checked_at stamps (1 s resolution); the cloud receipt has no phase timings.
cloud_measurement.fit: seconds = 2.80 + 0.455 x new_articles (10 members). Residuals within +/-4 s; BE +3.2 s (largest evidence store, research history).
cloud_measurement.phase_split_inferred: Cloud does not record phases, so the split is inferred: about 2.8 s fixed per member (4 Longbridge calls + 2 RSS feeds in sequence with local work; local work alone is 0.40 s/member without news on the benchmark (--no-news, N=10, registers 4 price records/member), so about 2 s is network wait) plus about 0.46 s per newly registered article (registration, manifest rewrite, text index). Per-phase cloud timing needs the phase fields added to the receipt (KARST-256).
cloud_measurement.window_note: 8 of 10 members used a 3-day news window because they have no research baseline and no 'unchanged' check; BE and AXTI used their last check / research time.

projection_200.method: Cloud fit per member x 200, plus the two quadratic terms from the local benchmark (index_store, checkpoint), members sequential as today.

news_day_like_2026_09_22.basis: 200 x (2.80 + 0.455 x 14.5 mean articles) = 1,880 s; + about 45 s index_store growth and 6 s checkpoint at N=200; index_store grows further with accumulated evidence

prices_only_floor.basis: 200 x 2.8 s fixed cost + quadratic terms; even with zero new articles

local_cpu_only.basis: benchmark N=200 with zero injected delay

projection_200.against_targets: Targets are <= 5 min prices+technicals and <= 10 min with news for 200, and <= 60 s per MCP call. Today: about 10 min price-only floor and about 32 min on a news day; one MCP call for 10 members already takes 95 s. None met.

bottlenecks_ranked.what: Members run strictly one after another, so every network wait adds up
bottlenecks_ranked.evidence: Cloud fixed cost about 2.8 s/member of which about 2 s is waiting; delayed benchmark: 90 s of 136 s is injected wait, added one-for-one. At 200 members this alone is about 9-10 min.
bottlenecks_ranked.lever: bounded parallelism with per-source rate limits; fetch only new bars

bottlenecks_ranked.what: Evidence registration re-reads, re-validates and rewrites each company's whole manifest (with fsync) for every single record
bottlenecks_ranked.evidence: Local: register_evidence + read_registry = 56% of time at N=10, 50% at N=200; 3,400 manifest reads for 2,000 records. Cloud: 0.455 s per new article (MSFT 73 articles = 37 s of the 95 s run).
bottlenecks_ranked.lever: register one refresh's records in one batch (one manifest read and one write per company per run)

bottlenecks_ranked.what: Full-text index duplicate check scans the whole FTS table
bottlenecks_ranked.evidence: index_store per member 31 -> 74 -> 236 ms as N goes 10 -> 50 -> 200 (quadratic total); grows further with every day of stored evidence.
bottlenecks_ranked.lever: keep evidence_id existence in an indexed ordinary table (or rowid map) instead of querying the FTS5 column

bottlenecks_ranked.what: Checkpoint and MCP response carry the entire receipt every time
bottlenecks_ranked.evidence: 156 MB serialized for one N=200 run (1.5 MB final); cloud 10-member response 246 KB already overflowed the client tool-result limit; 200 real members would be several MB.
bottlenecks_ranked.lever: append per-member results (or per-subject files) and return a summary plus run_id

bottlenecks_ranked.evidence: plan_update runs twice per member (inside refresh_sources and again in daily.refresh) and loads the research protocol 4 times; packet rewrite 50 ms/member. Together about 70 ms/member locally: small, linear.
bottlenecks_ranked.lever: run plan_update once per member, cache the protocol digest

not_bottlenecks: Series rebuild from all price evidence is 8 ms/member locally with 1000 bars and flat in N; peak memory under 90 MB.
limits: Local timings are Windows file-system costs (fsync heavy); Linux cloud per-record cost differs, which is why the cloud fit, not the local numbers, drives the 200 projection.
Cloud per-member times have 1-second resolution and one day's news mix; a quieter day lowers the news term, not the 2.8 s fixed cost.
The fake Longbridge returns small JSON bodies; real candle responses and SDK latency are inside the cloud fixed cost.
